The **OperatingSystem** standard library checks the disk: whether files and
directories exist, what they contain, and the process environment. This part's
workspace ships a `sample_data/` folder of fixtures — a log, a CSV, config, and
XML — to work against. Keywords like `File Should Exist`, `Directory Should Exist`,
`Set Environment Variable`, and `Environment Variable Should Be Set` make good
preconditions: assert the data is there before a test uses it.

## Task 1 — Assert the sample data files and an environment variable

**Goal:** create `checks/files.robot` that imports `OperatingSystem`, asserts the
sample data is present, sets an environment variable, and checks it is set.

Here is the same set of checks over a different file and variable. Adapt them.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    OperatingSystem

*** Test Cases ***
Log File Is Present
    File Should Exist    sample_data/app.log
    Directory Should Exist    sample_data
    Set Environment Variable    SHOP_REGION    eu
    Environment Variable Should Be Set    SHOP_REGION
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the suite imports `OperatingSystem` and defines `Sample Data Is Present`.

<!-- hint -->
Assert two files this time: `File Should Exist    sample_data/catalog.xml` and
`File Should Exist    sample_data/orders.csv`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Set and verify your own variable — pick any name, e.g.
`Set Environment Variable    SHOP_ENV    test` then
`Environment Variable Should Be Set    SHOP_ENV`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    OperatingSystem

*** Test Cases ***
Sample Data Is Present
    File Should Exist    sample_data/catalog.xml
    File Should Exist    sample_data/orders.csv
    Directory Should Exist    sample_data
    Set Environment Variable    SHOP_ENV    test
    Environment Variable Should Be Set    SHOP_ENV
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the files, directory, and environment variable all check out.
